newsitem.title: UK: Tung urges Blair to take new line on Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Tung urges Blair to take new line on Hong Kong.

text.p: Tung Chee-Hwa, to be Hong Kong's chief executive after the British colony's handover to Beijing next month, has urged new Labour Prime Minister Tony Blair to make a new start in Sino-British relations.

In an interview with foreign correspondents quoted in the British media on Tuesday, he laid the blame for friction between London and Beijing on "the last Conservative government. There were major changes. This was very unfortunate".
Chris Patten, Hong Kong's 28th and final governor after 156 years of British rule, has angered Beijing in the runup to the handover by championing civil rights.
Tung said: "I hope the new Labour government will look at the whole issue in a more macro way, looking at long-term relations between Hong Kong and Britain, China and Britain."
He urged it to "put behind us all the arguments, to sit down, to say these things have to be done and move forward continuously in the interest of the six and half million people of Hong Kong."
Britain's new Foreign Secretary Robin Cook said on Monday that Hong Kong's smooth handover to China on June 30 was one of the Labour government's top priorities.
After telephoning Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten, Cook pledged his support for human rights in the colony.
